clue.text: Prior, clergyman that's outwardly sanctimonious

indicators.note: outwardly says the sanctimonious word sits on the outside, wrapping the clergyman

parts.note: sanctimonious means pious, showily devout
Rev is the short title for a reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A monastic prior is described as a cleric who looks holy on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' looks like the head of a priory, but it is the adjective meaning earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior and previous are synonyms meaning coming before in time.

clue.text: Section of band that may have blues accompaniment?

definitions.text: Section of band that may have blues accompaniment?

parts.words: Section of band that may have blues accompaniment?
parts.note: the ... section of a band, and the R in R and B, a style paired with blues

explanation.surface: A part of a band might be backed by the blues.
explanation.walkthrough: A band's rhythm section is its drums and bass, and the music R&B pairs this word with blues.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhythm section is the part of a band keeping the beat, and rhythm and blues is a genre.

clue.text: Some devil erupts, getting more unpleasant

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small devil bursts out as things turn nastier.
explanation.definitionFit: Viler is the comparative of vile, so more nasty or more unpleasant.

clue.text: Unfashionable clothes seen in suburbia

parts.note: something out is no longer in fashion
skirts are items of clothing

explanation.surface: Dated clothing is spotted in the suburbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Suburbia lies on the outer fringes of a town, its edges or outlying districts.

clue.text: I have withdrawn from repeated achievement

indicators.note: withdrawn from says the I have contraction is pulled out of the repeated word

parts.note: successive means following one after another, repeated
I've is the contracted form of I have

explanation.surface: Someone pulls out of a string of triumphs.
explanation.walkthrough: SUCCESSIVE loses its ending IVE, the contraction of I have.
explanation.definitionFit: A success is an accomplishment or achievement.

clue.text: Fawn overturned cooking pot — drag!

indicators.note: overturned says the word for the cooking pot is turned backwards

parts.note: a wok is a Chinese cooking pot
to drag something is to tow it

explanation.surface: Someone knocks over a cooking pot and finds the whole business a drag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fawn' looks like a young deer or a colour, but it is the verb meaning to grovel.
explanation.definitionFit: To fawn and to kowtow both mean to behave with servile, grovelling deference.

clue.text: Cloth that's uniformly used

parts.note: a drab dust-coloured cloth that is used for military uniforms, so used in uniform

explanation.walkthrough: 'uniformly' looks like evenly, but it means in uniforms.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is a sturdy brownish fabric used for army uniforms.

clue.text: Method of printing internet from TV

parts.note: the web is the internet
off can mean from, as in to take off the table
a TV set is a television

explanation.surface: Printing methods are drawn from the internet and television.
explanation.definitionFit: Web offset is offset lithography printed on a continuous roll of paper, a printing technique.

clue.text: Speaker I love that's set to music

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: A public speaker declares an affection that has been set to music.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large-scale sacred work set to music for voices and orchestra.

clue.text: Loophole gives viewer permit

parts.note: an eye is what views, so a viewer
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A gap in the rules hands someone watching a licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loophole' suggests a legal escape, but here it is a literal small hole for a lace or cord.
explanation.definitionFit: A loophole in its literal sense is a small opening, and an eyelet is a small hole for threading.

clue.text: Fabric taken from room without hesitation by Illingworth?

indicators.note: without says the hesitation sound is dropped from the room word

parts.note: a chamber is a room
er is the sound of someone hesitating
Ray Illingworth was an England cricket captain

explanation.surface: Some cloth is fetched from a room, without delay, by a cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray Illingworth was a Yorkshire and England cricketer, captain in the early 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambray is a light cotton cloth woven with a white weft and coloured warp, so a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Charlie Champion anxious to disregard final part as Native American

parts.note: Charlie is C in the radio alphabet
a champion is a hero

indicators.note: to disregard final part says the last letter of the anxious word is dropped

parts.note: anxious to do something is keen

explanation.surface: Charlie, a champion, is keen to ignore the ending of a story about a Native American.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cherokee are a Native American people of the south-eastern United States.

clue.text: Stream from outside home repelled beast

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: repelled says the beast word is driven back, so read backwards

parts.note: a wolf is a wild beast

explanation.surface: Someone from outside the house drives off a wild animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflow is a stream of something coming in, like water or money.

clue.text: Indications chap will have craft and skill in shooting

parts.note: marks are signs or indications
a chap is a man
a ship is a sailing craft

explanation.surface: Signs suggest a man will have the cunning and talent needed to shoot well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like cunning, paired with skill, but it is a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Marksmanship is the ability to hit a target accurately with a gun.

clue.text: It seemed to me Middle English needs to include common elements of 'thee' and 'thou'

parts.note: the letters shared by the two old pronouns are their opening T and H
ought means needs to, should

explanation.surface: An old poetic phrase is explained in Middle English, using the pronouns thee and thou.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts come in order ME, TH and OUGHT; 'include' only links them.
explanation.definitionFit: Methought is an archaic expression meaning I thought or it appeared to me.

clue.text: A chain found in Italy

parts.note: the Pennines are the chain of hills running down northern England

explanation.surface: A mountain range is located in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds: A plus the English hill chain gives the Italian range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the mountain range running down the length of the Italian peninsula.

clue.text: Ten going in to clear entrance in the nearest house

indicators.note: going in to says ten is placed inside the clear word

parts.note: net means clear, as in net profit after deductions
X is the Roman numeral for ten
a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: Ten people pass through to clear the doorway of the neighbouring house.
explanation.definitionFit: Next door is an idiom for the adjoining house, the one nearest to one's own.

clue.text: Novel with moving statement, part of good book

parts.note: novel means new

indicators.note: moving says the letters of statement are shifted into another order

explanation.surface: A new novel contains a moving statement that forms part of a fine book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, but it is the adjective meaning new; STATEMENT rearranged gives TESTAMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Good Book is the Bible, and this is its second major division.

clue.text: A memorial of victory wasting away

parts.note: a trophy is a prize kept as a memento of winning

explanation.surface: A trophy from a past win is slowly falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrophy is the gradual withering of a body part or tissue through disuse or disease.

clue.text: Queen isn't commonly charming!

parts.note: ain't is the common, colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that the queen is not ordinary, but delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' looks like often, but it means in informal speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaint means attractively old-fashioned, charming in an unusual way.

clue.text: Tough street, sinful it's said

indicators.note: it's said marks that the sinful word is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: something sinful is wrong

explanation.surface: A rough street is said to be a wicked place.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, WRONG loses its silent W, so it gives only RONG after ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong and tough are synonyms for something robust and hard to break.

clue.text: Look, going round the bend, for dressing

indicators.note: going round says the look word is wrapped around the bend

parts.note: to gaze is to look
a U-bend is a bend shaped like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone looks while driving round a corner, on the way to a bandage.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauze is a thin open-weave fabric used as a medical dressing for wounds.

clue.text: With Jack collected, dismiss car

indicators.note: collected says the sailor is gathered up inside the dismissal word

parts.note: to run out a batsman is one way to dismiss him in cricket
a jack is a sailor, and AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: Once Jack has been picked up, someone says to get rid of the car.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a run out is a dismissal where the batsman is caught short of his ground; Jack and AB are both crossword sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: A runabout is a small light car suited to short trips.

clue.text: Bust of old boy set up — some but not all present

indicators.note: set up in a down clue says the old boy letters are raised, read upwards

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: but not all says the word some is cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: A sculpted bust of a former pupil is put up, though only some of the guests are there.
explanation.definitionFit: Bust and bosom are synonyms for the human chest, especially a woman's.

clue.text: Ache before spring field event

indicators.note: before puts the ache word ahead of the spring word

parts.note: to ache for something is to long for it
a spring is a jump

explanation.surface: An ache comes on ahead of the spring athletics season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season, but it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: The long jump is an athletics field event in which competitors leap for distance.

clue.text: Monster I sense swimming around?

indicators.note: swimming around says the letters of the words move about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone senses a monster swimming nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie is the nickname of the fabled Loch Ness Monster of Scotland.

clue.text: Squirm as explosive document's advanced

indicators.note: advanced says the document goes ahead of the explosive

parts.note: a writ is a legal document
HE is the abbreviation for high explosive

explanation.surface: Someone wriggles as an explosive file is pushed forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and squirm, as in pain.

clue.text: You initially see Tom travelling round one national park

indicators.note: initially says only the opening letter of You is taken
round says the mixed letters go around the word for one
travelling says the letters of see and Tom wander into a new order

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: You first see Tom touring a national park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' makes OSEMTE from SEE and TOM, and 'round' places it around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Yosemite in California is one of the best-known national parks in the United States.
